texts.preamble: Shri Amit Aggarwal vs State Through Food Safety Officer on 8 September, 2015 In The Court Of Shri Amar Nath District & Sessions Judge : New Delhi District : New Delhi Fsat Appeal No. 83/14 Shri Amit Aggarwal S/o Shri Parshotam Aggarwal R/o D18, Jain Colony, BlockD, Barwala, Delhi 110033 ....... Appellant Versus State through Food Safety Officer, Department of Food Safety, Govt. of Nct of Delhi A20, Lawrence Road, Industrial Area Delhi 110035 ......Respondent Date of Institution of Appeal : 22.12.2014 Judgment reserved on : 01.09.2015 Judgment announced on : 08.09.2015 Judgment
texts.facts: This appeal is directed against the order dated 25.11.2014 (hereinafter referred to as "Impugned Order") passed by Sh. Som Naidu, Ld. Adjudicating Officer/ADM (North), Govt. of NCT of Delhi whereby penalty of Rs. 40,000/ was imposed upon the appellant praying therein ; to [LEAKAGE_MASK] the impugned order. FSAT Appeal No. 83/2014 page no. 1 of 6 Amit Aggarwal Vs. FSO 2. The appeal was admitted. The notice of the appeal was given to the respondent who has resisted the same. The record of the Ld. Adjudicating Officer was requisitioned. Feeling aggrieved, the appellant has challenged the impugned order mainly on the following two grounds; a) Ld. Adjudicating Officer/ADM has failed to appreciate that the 'date of manufacture' or 'best before date' or 'expiry date' is not required to be mentioned on the package having surface area of less than 30 sq. centimeters but these information shall be mentioned on the wholesale packages or multipiece packages, as the case may be. The case of the prosecution in brief is that on 30.05.2013 at about 4 PM Food Safety Officer Ms. Usha Kiran went to the shop of Sh. Amit Aggarwal, FBO M/s Aggarwal Agency, Society, Bus Stand, Bawana Road, Delhi 110039 and purchased the sample of Pan Masala after FSAT Appeal No. 83/2014 page no. 2 of 6 Amit Aggarwal Vs. FSO paying Rs. 1200/ as its cost. Four sample packets were fastened, sealed and the signatures of FBO were obtained as per the prescribed procedure. The panchnama in Form VA prepared and the signature of the Food Business Operator (FBO) was obtained as the token of its acknowledgment. One sealed packet of the sample was sent to the food analyst, Delhi. On testing, it was not found to be adulterated, however, it was stated to be misbranding because the same was not having batch number and nutritional information on the label of the packet and hence, the appellant violated the Regulations 2.2.2.9 of the Food Safety and Standard (Packaging and Labelling) Regulation, 2011 (hereinafter to be referred 'FSSRs (Packaging and Labelling). Ld. Adjudicating officer did impose the penalty of Rs. 40,000/ on the report of Food Analyst. On receipt of the notice, the appellant appeared and filed reply of the complaint before Ld. Adjudicating Officer mentioning therein that the counter part of the sample be summoned to calculate the surface area of the pouch of Pan Masala.
texts.arguments: 6. First and foremost point raised by the Ld. Counsel for the appellant is that he is protected under the rules 2.6 of the FSSRs (Packaging and Labelling) which provides exemption from labeling requirements under 2.6.1 in sub clause (2). Per contra, the learned Special PP has refuted the entire line of arguments while making submissions that the Food Inspector was within its power to lift the sample of Pan Masala. He further stated that the date of manufacture or best before date or expiry date was required to be mentioned on the packets having surface area of even less than 30 sq. centimeter and as such it comes within the mischief of Section 16(1)(a) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (herein after referred to as "the Act"). Shri Amit Aggarwal vs State Through Food Safety Officer on 8 September, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64752698/ 2 8. His second line of argument is that the sample was taken on 30.05.2013 and the public analyst started the analysis on 03.06.2013 and completed the same on 08.06.2013 whereas he did sign the report on 10.06.2013 which apparently indicates the delay in signing the report of the public analyst and then the report would certainly lose the evidentiary value. To support his contention, he placed reliance upon the judgment as reported Delhi Administration Vs. Amar Chand, 2012 (3) JCC 1930 (DHC) wherein, the Lordship was pleased to make the following observations: Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 Public Analyst Report Sample was taken on 10.11.2005 and the Public Analyst completed the analysis on 17.11.2005 whereas he signed his report on 29.01.2005Delay in signing the report by the Public Analyst Reliance cannot be placed upon the report of the Public Analysis who analyzed the sample on 17.11.2005 and finalized by signing it on 29.11.2005. 9.
